facts.claim: On August 6, 2026, OpenAI, Amazon (AWS), Microsoft, Cursor (Anysphere), and Vercel simultaneously adopted Agent Plugins 1.0.0, a vendor-neutral packaging standard for AI agent skills and MCP servers.
Google joined as a core maintainer of Agent Plugins on the same day, August 6, 2026.
The standard is already integrated into VS Code, GitHub Copilot, Cursor, ChatGPT, and Kiro.
The steering committee for Agent Plugins spans AWS, Cursor maker Anysphere, Microsoft, OpenAI, and Vercel, with GitHub as an early collaborator.
Agent Plugins wraps MCP (Model Context Protocol) servers and Agent Skills into a single portable directory with a plugin.json manifest.
The standard defines two core components: Agent Skills (reusable, modular workflows) and MCP Servers (middleware connecting agents to external tools and APIs).
The 1.0 specification deliberately limits itself to packaging and discovery, leaving marketplaces, installation, permissions, sandboxing, and trust models to each client platform.
Anthropic was notably absent from the adopting companies.
The standard is positioned as an industry move that outpaced the IETF DAWN working group's governance debates.

Developer reactions are split: some celebrate the 'build once, run anywhere' promise, while others, including SST creator Dax Raad, express skepticism that the standard is thin and that useful parts will end up client-specific.
Developer advocate Angie Jones expressed support for the standard.
The standard collapses per-client packaging variants into one artifact that carries across supporting clients.
The original story received 24 points on Hacker News.

drafts.text: The Agent Plugins 1.0 spec is interesting precisely because of what it refuses to define: no permissions model, no sandboxing, no trust framework. Just a plugin.json manifest and a directory layout. That's not a bug. It means each platform competes on safety rather than on packaging format — and the IETF DAWN group is still debating governance while this already ships in VS Code and Copilot.

drafts.text: Most standards efforts try to specify everything and collapse under their own weight. Agent Plugins 1.0 took the opposite approach. The spec covers only packaging and discovery — one folder, one plugin.json. Permissions, sandboxing, trust, marketplaces: all deliberately left to the platforms. The result is something that already runs in ChatGPT, Copilot, Cursor, and VS Code while the IETF working group is still debating governance.

drafts.text: Agent Plugins 1.0 is a standard that wins by being small. Packaging and discovery only — no permissions, no trust model, no marketplace. I think that's the right call for now. You can't spec safety across six companies with different threat models, but you can agree on a folder layout. Anthropic sitting it out is the other story here.
